```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(cli.num_colors = 1L)
```

An async expression is split in two. Reactive reads that appear literally in
it, such as `input$x`, `input[["x"]]`, `rv$y`, `data()` or `mod$data()`, are
evaluated on the session thread, where they register dependencies as usual.
So are `req()`, `validate()`, `invalidateLater()`, `isolate()`,
`status_async()` and `has_value_async()`, whether written bare, as
`shiny::req()`, or through a module object as `shiny$req()`, the form
`box::use(shiny)` gives. Their values, together with any user-defined
functions and objects the expression refers to, are sent to a worker that
evaluates the rest. Packages attached in the session and used by the
expression, directly or through a helper it ships, are attached in the worker.

## Seeing the split

`print()` shows the split for an async reactive: the calls evaluated on the
session, the objects and packages shipped to the worker, and the rewritten
worker expression. Nothing is evaluated and the task is not started, so it
works outside a running app. Here a `reactiveValues()` stands in for `input`:

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(shinyasync)

input <- reactiveValues(x = "wt", B = 2000)
slope <- function(d, x) coef(lm(reformulate(x, "mpg"), d))[[2]]

slopes <- reactiveAsync(
  replicate(input$B, slope(mtcars[sample(nrow(mtcars), replace = TRUE), ], input$x))
)
print(slopes)
```

The `session` line lists the reads hoisted to placeholders, `shipped` the
helpers and objects serialized with each task, and `worker` the expression the
worker evaluates. A `resident` line lists names preloaded on the workers with
`pool_async(everywhere = )`, and a `missing` line lists functions the session
could not find.

In `shiny::devmode()` each async reactive prints itself on its first run, and
each `mirai_async()` call site the first time it runs in a session, without
the worker expression, so the console shows what every task shipped. Set
`options(shinyasync.print = FALSE)` to turn that off.

## Limits

These follow from capture working on the expression as written:

- **Packages must be attached in the session.** A function is found on the
  worker because the session found it: `GET()` is shipped as "attach httr"
  only if `library(httr)` ran in the session. A function the session cannot
  resolve warns on the first run, and `print()` lists it on a `missing` line;
  attach the package or write `httr::GET()`. Functions that only exist inside
  a data mask, such as `n()` in a `dplyr::summarise()` call when dplyr is not
  attached, trigger the same warning although they work.
- **Reads must be literal.** Reads inside helper functions or with computed
  names (`input[[paste0("x", i)]]`) cannot be resolved. Read such values in a
  separate `reactive()` first, or pass them with `globals = list(...)`.
- **Every read is a dependency**, even in a branch that is not taken:
  `if (input$a) input$b else 0` re-runs when `input$b` changes. Wrap a read in
  `isolate()` to use its value without depending on it.
- **`req()` and `validate()` run on the session** only when they are certain
  to run, that is not inside `if`, `&&`, `||`, `switch`, loops or functions,
  and not when they use variables created inside the expression. Otherwise
  they run in the worker, where a failure keeps the previous value.
- **Reads inside formulas are hoisted**, so `lm(y ~ input$x)` fits on the
  value of `input$x` under a placeholder name. Other formula symbols are
  shipped if they name a plain object in the session.
- **Assigning to reactive values** (`rv$x <- ...`) inside the expression is an
  error. Do that in an `observe()` that reads the result.
- **Shipped objects are sent on every run.** A session object the expression
  refers to is serialized with every task, so a large data frame at the top of
  `app.R` costs its size on every invalidation. Load such objects once on
  every worker with `pool_async(everywhere = )` instead; the names it creates
  are *resident* and left out of what a task ships, whether the expression
  uses them directly or through a helper it ships. See
  `vignette("deployment")`.
- **An upstream `reactiveAsync()` is waited for.** A downstream keeps its
  previous value while an upstream it reads catches up; the rules, including
  the `bindEvent()` cases, are under "Chained async reactives" in
  `vignette("shinyasync")`.

## Reporting a capture problem

Capture rewrites your expression, so it can get a case wrong. If an
expression works in a plain `reactive()` but fails or behaves differently in
`reactiveAsync()`, please open an
[issue](https://github.com/dawiegriesel/shinyasync/issues) with the
expression and the output of `print()` on it.
